verified.analysis: The event survives strict gating: a named 5.0% holder, six named nominees, a company-confirmed nomination notice, competing WHITE/BLUE cards, and a hard dated vote roughly three months out - and it is structurally unusual because ETD's board is unclassified with all six seats (one currently vacant) elected annually, so a single vote can sweep control rather than settle for two seats. Provenance holds where it usually breaks: there is no preferred stack, no funded debt, and no external manager, so unlike FIP the common captures 100% of any value created; the $127.9M of cash and investments ($5.03/sh) and $313M of owned PP&E under a $579M cap give a real asset floor, and the stock at ~1.35x tangible book with a ~6-7% dividend pays you to wait. Two things cap this at 6 rather than 7+: G3 fails on check - Bergeron demands growth, digital execution and CEO succession but no sale, breakup or asset monetization, so there is no contractual or derivable re-rate figure, and his one hard number ($187.5M liquidity) is ~$60M stale against the year-end sheet filed four business days before his letter; and the win condition is a multi-year operational turnaround of a brand whose revenue has fallen ~46% from its 2006 peak, against a board that already beat back a 2015 proxy contest with the same CEO surviving. Offsetting that, residual capture is as close to untouched as this screen ever sees - the stock is below its pre-announcement price, so nothing is harvested; the risk is that the vote is won and the business still does not re-rate, which is why I size this as a cheap asset-backed cyclical carrying a free option on a board sweep, not as an event trade.
